stories.name: Apple Q3 earnings
stories.blurb: Apple's fiscal Q3 earnings report and the debate over whether the stock's record highs and AI-driven valuation are justified.

stories.name: Apple Broadcom chip deal
stories.blurb: Apple has extended and expanded its multibillion-dollar deal with Broadcom to supply U.S.-made wireless chips through 2031, including a major expansion of Broadcom's Colorado factory.

stories.name: Apple Foldable iPhone Launch
stories.blurb: Apple debuts its first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, at a launch event marking John Ternus's first showcase as CEO.

stories.name: Apple OpenAI trade secrets lawsuit
stories.blurb: Apple is suing OpenAI and former employees for allegedly stealing hardware trade secrets, a case OpenAI is fighting to dismiss.

stories.name: Meta's Muse AI Surge
stories.blurb: Meta's stock rallies as its new AI app Muse gains rapid popularity, boosting investor confidence in the company's AI strategy ahead of Meta Connect.

rel.why: Meta is a major Apple competitor in AI and consumer platforms, and its AI surge pressures Apple's own AI strategy and stock narrative.

stories.name: Qualcomm Apple patent deal
stories.blurb: Qualcomm and Apple renewed their long-term global patent licensing agreement, easing investor fears about Qualcomm's revenue but leaving questions about its growth beyond Apple.

rel.why: Qualcomm is a key Apple supplier whose renewed patent license and royalty deal directly affects Apple's costs and iPhone modem plans.

stories.name: iPhone 18 demand concerns
stories.blurb: Analysts and investors are scrutinizing early iPhone 18 pre-order and wait-time data for signs of weak or mixed consumer demand, weighing on Apple's stock.

past.name: Vanguard Growth ETF Debate
past.blurb: A recurring theme of financial articles comparing and recommending Vanguard growth-focused ETFs (like VUG and VGT) against rivals as long-term investment options.

past.name: Iran-Israel Oil Market Swings
past.blurb: Stock markets fluctuate as investors react to escalating and de-escalating US-Iran/Middle East tensions, oil price swings, and their effects on earnings, Fed policy, and economic data.

past.name: Memory Chip Shortage
past.blurb: A global surge in memory and storage chip prices is forcing Apple to raise prices on MacBooks and iPads while even considering banned Chinese chip suppliers to cope with the shortage.

7.text: Apple stock rose 31% over twelve months and 25% year-to-date, closing at $333.69, with analysts split—some raising targets, others cutting. Square integrated Apple Maps, Siri, and Wallet; Apple's consensus target sits below its price despite $63 billion net cash.

13.text: Broadcom is being compared favorably to Applied Materials and Marvell as a 2026 semiconductor investment, citing its $63.9B revenue and major tech partnerships. Apple is not mentioned, so the articles bear on it only as one of Broadcom's reported partners.

8.text: John Ternus became Apple's CEO and is restructuring management to speed product launches. Apple's foldable iPhone Duo, priced at $1,999, is projected by Counterpoint to sell 6 million units this year, though analysts question sustained demand beyond early adopters.

6.text: Apple Pay launched in India with Axis Bank cards, and a California Apple Pay fees lawsuit became a class action. Apple and Amazon face a UK consumer lawsuit, while Musk’s X and SpaceXAI dropped their antitrust claims against Apple.

11.text: Meta's Muse AI agent launched September 8 and became the top free iPhone app in the U.S., beating ChatGPT in Apple iOS downloads and driving Meta stock up roughly 13% weekly and over 30% monthly. Meta is now expanding Muse to small businesses, though no quarter including Muse has been reported yet.

12.text: Qualcomm renewed its global patent license agreement with Apple, effective April 1, 2027, covering Apple's continued access to Qualcomm's cellular technology. Qualcomm stock fell on profit-taking and Samsung 2nm pricing tensions, while Amazon became a new data center customer.

14.text: Jefferies flagged softer iPhone 18 demand after Hong Kong resale prices for high-end models fell below last year's levels. Counterpoint reported iPhone 18 Pro China launch-week sales rose 12% year-over-year, giving Apple the top smartphone market share there.

10.text: Bernstein warned that rising memory chip costs pose downside risk to Apple's December-quarter results, though it kept its Outperform rating and $370 price target.
